detail: Example equations mix plain numbers with a {rate:}/{duration:} result, so they break when a reader picks hours. Compiled HTML shows these in hour mode: credit "15 × 2 = 600 credits per hour" (the sentence above it says 40 credits per hour); mobility "20 × 8 × 0.1 = 320 credits per hour" (the line above it says 2 credits per hour); game-time "20 × 24 = 24 hours". Only the result converts, the factors do not. All three pages break this way on the public site with ?unit=hour, and in game for any player whose Income display is set to per hour.
proposed_fix: credit (owner of taxes): write "a system with 15 workforce pays 15 × {rate:system_population_taxes_factor|credits} = {rate:30|credits}", so both sides convert. mobility (owner of the mobility example): "20 workforce × 8 mobility × {rate:system_mobility_taxes_factor|credits} = {rate:16|credits}". game-time: drop the multiplication and write "A month has 20 calendar days and a year has 24 months. A calendar year lasts {duration:480}."

detail: One quantity has two names on the same page. The generated table's column says "Victory points", but the prose says "Each class is worth a number of System points" ({ui:panel.help.legend_mode_population_name}) and then just "the points". The {name:victory.population} token also renders as "Path of Influence", so the sentence reads "its score on the Path of Influence victory path" ("path" twice, and bold markup leaks in from the name).
proposed_fix: population-class: say once that the table's Victory points are what the game calls System points, for example "The Victory points column is shown in game as {ui:panel.help.legend_mode_population_name}." Or ask the population_classes generator to label the column with that UI token. Rewrite the victory sentence as "That total is its score for {name:victory.population}." Report the <strong> inside the name string to the compiler/token owner.

detail: The guide's chart story (housing=40, bonus=0) says the zero-bonus colony "stops below its target" because "growth stops when stability runs out". The chart sets stability = 35 + bonus − floor(population) (charts.ex:88-93), so that line settles at 36 population with stability flickering between 0 and −1. That is Discontentment (−10 % outputs) on the population-status table. The guide never mentions or links population-status or system-penalties in its prose. A player who follows the chart's most likely scenario is not told the system is penalized, and would have to go guide → stability → population-status → system-penalties (four pages) to learn why outputs dropped.
proposed_fix: population (guide): after "growth stops when stability runs out", add one sentence: "At 0 stability or below, the system also gets a [[population-status]] that reduces its outputs." No other page changes.

detail: No page in this run links [[game-time]], yet every rate renders as "per tick" or "per hour" ({rate:} renders a plain span, not a link). A player who opens credit, mobility or stability from a ? button cannot find out what a tick is or why the numbers change with speed. game-time is reachable only from the index or glossary.
proposed_fix: credit (the first guide with a rate): add after the taxes rate "Rates are per tick or per hour. See [[game-time]]." Better for the whole manual: have the compiler render the unit word inside {rate:}/{duration:} as a link to game-time, or print a footer link on every speed_sensitive page. Owner: credit, or the compiler (RC.Help).

detail: The over-mobilization formula appears on two pages. workforce has "penalty = 1 − workforce ÷ mobilized" in its indented block, and system-penalties repeats it as the Size cell ("1 − workforce ÷ mobilized"). The same 12/15 → 20 % example is also on both pages. The guide map gives the formula to workforce. system-penalties only needs to state size and point back.
proposed_fix: system-penalties: change the Size cell to "the share over-mobilized, see [[workforce]]" and keep the 12/15 line only as the first step of the combine example. workforce keeps the formula.

detail: The system-penalties combine example types "{name:population_status.demonstration} (25 %)". That restates a row of the population_statuses table, which lives on population-status, as a hand-typed literal. population_status.ex is not in system-penalties' sources (rules 10 and 11). If the Protests penalty changes, the example silently goes stale.
proposed_fix: system-penalties: drop the typed "(25 %)" and write "also {name:population_status.demonstration}: 120 − 25 % = 90", with lib/data/game/content/population_status.ex added to sources. Or replace the percentage with a token if the compiler exposes one for status penalties.

detail: One penalty gets glossary entries on two pages. workforce's terms carry "over-mobilization" while system-penalties' terms carry "over-mobilized population" (the tooltip label for the same thing). system-penalties also claims "insufficient stability", which is the tooltip label population-status explains ("Tooltips show this penalty as Insufficient stability"). The generated glossary will send near-identical words to different pages.
proposed_fix: Move "over-mobilized population" to workforce's terms (next to over-mobilization) and "insufficient stability" to population-status's terms. system-penalties keeps "system penalties", "output penalty" and "besieged".

detail: The growth target is named two ways. The guide says "Housing sets the target: housing + 0.75" and "A system above its target shrinks back". The housing leaf, and so the guide's "Pages in this guide" blurb, says "Housing is the population a system grows toward", which reads as the target being housing itself. The guide's own screenshot caption also says "negative here because population is above housing" rather than above its target.
proposed_fix: housing: "Housing sets the population a system grows toward." (keep "See [[population]] for how growth uses it."). population: caption "...negative here because population is above its growth target."

detail: The housing leaf names the per-planet share {name:bonus_pipeline_in.body_pop} ("Local Population"), which is also the name used in the buildings_by_input body_pop table. Its example block then calls the same values "13 population" and "3 population", as if they were system population.
proposed_fix: housing: change the example lines to "planet with 13 housing from buildings: 13 {name:bonus_pipeline_in.body_pop}" and "planet with 3 housing from buildings: 3 {name:bonus_pipeline_in.body_pop}".

detail: The two sibling credit examples use different bases for the same thing. credit's taxes example says "a system with 15 population pays 15 × 2", while mobility's example says "a system with 20 workforce". Code multiplies both taxes and mobility by state.workforce (stellar_system.ex:1833-1834), and credit itself says "Whole points of population are the system's workforce". Saying "15 population" invites a player with 15.8 population to expect 31.6.
proposed_fix: credit: write the taxes example with "15 workforce" (combine with the hour-mode fix above).

detail: Two first sentences define overlapping mood words differently. stability says it is "how content a system's population is", and population-status says a status "tells how calm a system's population is". A reader of the guide's leaf list sees two blurbs for what sounds like the same measure, and the status is really a tier derived from stability.
proposed_fix: population-status: "A population status is the tier a system's [[stability]] puts it in." (the table follows). stability keeps its definition.
